rebuttal_or_critique: I find the continued insistence on a 'withdrawal of accommodation' stance increasingly disconnected from the macroeconomic reality. With core inflation at a benign 3.10%, the current repo rate of 6.50% implies a real policy rate that is significantly restrictive. My colleagues emphasize food inflation at 8.69%, but monetary policy is a blunt instrument that cannot address supply-side food price volatility without inflicting unnecessary damage on the broader growth momentum of 6.80%. Maintaining a restrictive stance when the output gap is only marginally positive at 0.40% risks over-tightening and stifling the recovery. We must shift to a neutral stance to reflect that the policy rate is already sufficiently high to anchor expectations without acting as a drag on the economy.
